metadata.title: Why Only 0.7% of a Cancer Nanoparticle Reaches the Tumor
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer of Cancer Nanomedicine candidate 02. Source chapter: cancer-nanomedicine/chapters/01-what-counts-as-cancer-nanomedicine.md (the dose-loss chain / delivery funnel mechanism only).
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL #1F6F5C = dose reaching tumor / surviving dose; CRIMSON #BF3339 = lost dose / each loss step; GOLD #F5D061 = the 0.7% number. Never swapped mid-film.
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: NO DLS/TEM, NO polydispersity, NO two-liposomes case, NO EPR mechanism detail, NO 0.7% metric debate. One mechanism only: the delivery funnel — five sequential loss steps between syringe and tumor cell.

props.segment: Why Only 0.7% of a Cancer Nanoparticle…
props.command: Why Only 0.7% of a Cancer Nanoparticle Reaches the Tumor?

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. A researcher injects a dose of tumor-targeted nanoparticles into a mouse. Only 0.7 percent reaches the tumor. The other 99.3 percent goes somewhere else.

items.label: The dose
items.sub: Tumor-targeted nanoparticles injected into a mouse

items.label: The tumor
items.sub: Reached by only 0.7% of the injected dose

items.label: The gap
items.sub: The other 99.3% ends up somewhere else in the body

beats.narration_text: The particle was designed carefully. It carries a targeting ligand that binds receptors overexpressed on cancer cells. In cell culture it kills at a fraction of the normal dose.

items.label: Targeting ligand
items.sub: Binds receptors overexpressed on cancer cells

items.label: Cancer-cell receptors
items.sub: Overexpressed vs. healthy tissue — a real handle

items.label: In cell culture
items.sub: Kills at a fraction of the normal dose

beats.narration_text: So why does so little arrive? A tumor-targeted nanoparticle is injected into the bloodstream. The targeting ligand is working. And still, only 0.7 percent reaches the tumor.

props.title: So why does so little arrive?

items.label: Injected
items.sub: Nanoparticle enters the bloodstream at full dose

items.label: Ligand works
items.sub: Binding is happening — chemistry is on-spec

items.label: Yet 0.7%
items.sub: Is all that reaches the tumor — where does the rest go?

beats.narration_text: Because between the syringe and the tumor cell, the dose is lost at every step. Not one step — five sequential steps. Fail at any of them and the particle delivers nothing.

props.title: Five sequential steps — syringe to cell

items.label: Every step
items.sub: Dose is lost between syringe and tumor cell

items.label: Not one — five
items.sub: Five sequential losses, in a fixed order

items.label: Fail any
items.sub: The particle delivers nothing at all

beats.narration_text: Step one: survive circulation. The liver and spleen clear foreign particles from the blood within minutes. Most of the dose never gets a second chance.

items.label: Liver + spleen
items.sub: Clear foreign particles within minutes of injection

items.label: Most of dose
items.sub: Never gets a second chance at the tumor

items.label: First filter
items.sub: The dose falls before any later step can act

beats.narration_text: Step two: escape the vessel. Particles must exit the bloodstream into tumor tissue through leaky vessel walls. Many degrade or get trapped before they can.

items.label: Exit needed
items.sub: Cross from bloodstream into tumor tissue

items.label: Leaky walls
items.sub: Fenestrations are the only crossing point

items.label: Degrade or trapped
items.sub: Many fail before they can extravasate

beats.narration_text: Steps three, four, and five: penetrate the dense tumor matrix, get taken up by cells, and release the payload inside. Each step cuts the arriving dose again.

items.label: Penetrate
items.sub: Through dense tumor matrix — the stromal barrier

items.label: Cell uptake
items.sub: Cancer cell must actively engulf the particle

items.label: Release payload
items.sub: Drug must leave the particle inside the cell

beats.narration_text: Adding a targeting ligand only helps at step four — cell uptake. A particle that fails step one, cleared from circulation in the first hour, never reaches step four.

items.label: Step 4 helped
items.sub: The ligand acts on cell uptake — nothing earlier

items.label: Fail step 1
items.sub: Cleared in the first hour — never reaches step 4

items.label: Early loss dominates
items.sub: Upstream failure kills the late fix

beats.narration_text: The particle was not misbehaving. The targeting ligand was binding correctly. The delivery chain failed upstream, long before the ligand had any role.

props.title: The chain failed before the ligand mattered

items.label: Not misbehaving
items.sub: The particle worked as designed

items.label: Ligand binding
items.sub: Correctly locking onto its receptor target

items.label: Failed upstream
items.sub: Long before the ligand had any role to play

beats.narration_text: Take 100 illustrative units. Eighteen are cleared by spleen and liver in hour one. Fourteen more degrade in circulation. Twelve exit the vessel but cannot penetrate the matrix. Fifty-five reach non-tumor tissue. One unit — 0.7 — reaches the tumor and releases payload.

items.label: 32 cleared/degrade
items.sub: Spleen and liver in hour 1, plus circulation losses

items.label: 12 blocked
items.sub: Exit vessel but cannot penetrate the tumor matrix

items.label: 55 off-target
items.sub: Reach non-tumor tissue — 0.7 reach the tumor

beats.narration_text: A perfect targeting ligand solves one step of five. The funnel leaks everywhere upstream. Until those steps are measured and fixed, 0.7 percent is the answer.

props.title: The funnel leaks upstream — 0.7% is the answer

items.label: One of five
items.sub: A perfect ligand solves step 4 — nothing upstream

items.label: Leaks upstream
items.sub: Steps 1-3 dominate the loss no matter the ligand

items.label: Until measured
items.sub: 0.7% is the answer until the earlier steps are fixed

beats.narration_text: The verdict. Between the syringe and the tumor cell, dose is lost at five sequential steps: circulation clearance, vessel escape, matrix penetration, cell uptake, and payload release. The targeting ligand only helps at step four. On an illustrative one-hundred-unit dose, about thirty-two units clear or degrade in the bloodstream, twelve escape the vessel but cannot cross the matrix, and fifty-five land in non-tumor tissue. Zero point seven reach the tumor. The particle isn't misbehaving. The delivery chain fails upstream.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take a targeted therapy you are working on and walk it through the five-step funnel: circulation, extravasation, matrix penetration, cell uptake, release. Which step do you have measured, and which are you assuming?
